title: Spreadsheet: Roundtrip of setting the background color of a cell raises `TypeError`
input_version: current first body field, not edit history
problem_excerpt:
If you use the following code on a spreadsheet cell, which has the default background colour 
```python3
spreadsheet.setBackground('A1', spreadsheet.getBackground('A1'))
```
raises
```python3
TypeError: Tuple required.
```

This happens, because `spreadsheet.getBackground(cell)` returns `None` for a cell, which background colour is the default background. It would be good, if `spreadsheet.setBackground(cell, None)` resets the cell's background to the default colour.
invariants: default None resets; nondefault RGB unchanged

title: [Problem] Text and dimensions within BLOCKs are lost in DXF import
input_version: current first body field, not edit history
problem_excerpt:
Non-shape objects such as text and dimensions which exist in BLOCK definitions are not imported by the DXF importer.

A copy of them should be included each time the block is INSERTed, though the scaling of the object may be imperfect. I'm not certain for instance how scaling of the insert affects the text size of objects within the block.
scope: DXF BLOCK nonshape copies at INSERT
invariants: include text/dimensions every insert; scale behavior unsettled

title: [Problem] During C++ DXF import, the Group Layers option is not well handled
input_version: current first body field, not edit history
problem_excerpt:
During C++ DXF import, if "group layers" is selected, the shape contents of each layer are combined into a single shape, which is named using the layer name, and placed as a top-level object in the document. Non-shape contents (text, dimensions) are placed as individual objects at the top level since they can't be merged.

If the layer contains text etc. both the text and the merged shape should be placed in a Layer in the document. Only if there is just a single merged shape would that shape appear as a top-level object, duplicating existing behaviour.

If this option is not selected, such objects remain as individual un-merged shapes, but are still placed at the root level of the document. They should be placed in an appropriate Layer within the document, along with any text and dimensions within that layer.
scope: C++ DXF import grouping and tree
invariants: shape-only grouped layer stays top-level; mixed/ungrouped children and layer names preserved

title: [Feature] Sketcher: curves defined by equations
input_version: current first body field, not edit history
problem_excerpt:
Curves defined by equations are used when features follow precise mathematical definitions, like cams or involute profiles. There should be two kind of curves:

* normal functions like y = f(x) or x = f(y);
* parametric curves like x(t) = g1(t), y(t)=g2(t).

Several levels can be implemented:

1. Use the sketch origin as the equation origin, and base units.
2. Allow the user to select a point in sketch as the origin of the equation.
3. Allow the user to set the length of the unit.
4. Allow the user to have different x and y units.
5. Allow the user to define the full range of the curve using a rectangle.
6. Allow the user to define the axis of the equation (the rectangle of the previous point is rotated).
7. Allow the user to make the two axis at an arbitrary angle. I don’t know if this one is useful but who knows.

In any case:

* It should be possible to constrain geometry to this curve (make points coincident with it, lines tangent to it, etc).
* It should be possible to use variables in the equation, like named dimensions or values from a spreadsheet.
* It should be possible to edit the curve after it is created.
* It should be possible to re-limit the curve to use just a portion of it (the rest remains construction geometry or is hidden).
invariants: ordinary/parametric functions, constraints, variables, editability, trim retains definition

title: Android: Export should save data on SD card prior to sharing
input_version: current first body field, not edit history
problem_excerpt:
1. Open the Joplin Android app
2. Select configure / settings
3. Select Export
4. Tap Export all Notes as JEX (Alle Notizen als JEX exportieren)
5. Depending on the duration it takes a long time, then
6. A share dialog opens
7. The exported file is not stored as a backup

* Steps are translated from Germna

### Expected behaviour

I was trying to migrate my notes from one WebDAV URL to another using the Android app. Following the advice I tried to create a backup of all notes and I figured it would be stored somewhere.

- I just hit "Export all notes as JEX"
- it took a few minutes
- probably I missed the share dialog and assumed the backup file will be stored somewhere
- I lost four days of personal notes

It would be good to actually store the file locally (e.g. on SD card) *before* offering a share dialog, so that in every case a backup exists.
invariants: durable local JEX before optional share; cancellation leaves backup

title: docker-compose.server.yml shoud not expose Postgres port 5432 publicly
input_version: current first body field, not edit history
problem_excerpt:
The Joplin Server configuration in `docker-compose.server.yml` does not need to (and should not) expose port 5432 publicly. In Compose, containers that -- like Postgres -- expose ports can be reached by service-to-service communication inside the Compose network via that port. Thus, additionally exposing the Postgres server publicly might raise security issues, because the database server can be accessed directly (possibly from the internet, when no firewall is active).

Additionally, when using a reverse proxy (like Jason Wilder's nginx-proxy or Trafaek) it is even not necessary to expose port 22300 publicly. Reason: For the proxy-internal network this port is available as well (see explanation above). Thus, the reverse proxy just must be made to use this port (e.g. for nginx-proxy by setting the environment variable VIRTUAL_PORT=22300).

### Expected behaviour

The section "`ports`" should be removed from the service "`db`" in `docker-compose.server.yml`.

Optional: The section "`ports`" should be removed from the service "`app`" in `docker-compose.server.yml` (when using a reverse proxy and not accessing the server directly via port 22300).
invariants: internal DB reachable; no public DB port; proxy/direct access distinction
